This is a full-time, exempt position that can be hybrid or remote. Hybrid employees will be based in either our Melville, NY or Markham, Ontario, Canada office, with a combination of in-office and remote work. Standard hours are Monday through Friday during core business hours. Given the global nature of this role and the 24/7 support model, flexibility is expected to collaborate with teams in Canada and India, and contract resources worldwide, across significant time zone differences, including early-morning or late-day calls to overlap with the India team. Occasional availability outside standard hours may be required for major incidents, outages, and maintenance windows.

Travel

This position may require occasional domestic and international travel (approximately 10%) for team visits, vendor meetings, industry conferences, and cross-functional leadership engagements.

Required Education and Experience

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field; Master's degree or MBA preferred
* 15+ years of progressive experience in IT operations, systems administration, and/or technical support, including at least 7 years in a senior leadership or executive role (director level or above)
* Proven track record managing globally distributed technical teams, including onshore and offshore employees and contract resources, in a SaaS or enterprise software environment
* Demonstrated experience owning customer support and incident management for mission-critical applications, including SLA/SLO management, post-mortems, RCA, and executive service reporting
* Deep experience with employee enablement tools, including Microsoft 365, Entra, and Teams
* Extensive experience with cloud computing and infrastructure management
* Experience owning observability and monitoring platforms (such as Datadog, CloudWatch, Grafana, or equivalent) and building a metrics-driven approach to operational health
* Working knowledge of ITSM platforms (such as Jira Service Management) and frameworks such as ITIL, and of data analytics tools for performance monitoring
* Experience managing operations budgets for staffing, tooling, and vendors

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience leading technical operations and support at a SaaS or cloud-native company serving enterprise customers
* Experience overseeing technical support or IT staff in India, and managing contract and vendor-supplied resources
* ITIL certification (ITIL 4 Foundation or higher) and hands-on experience administering Jira Service Management
* Experience with AI-based automation for ticket triage, incident response, and self-healing, and familiarity with AI risk and responsible-use frameworks
* Experience in travel technology, hospitality, or other high-volume, customer-facing SaaS environments

Compensation:

The good faith compensation is $200,000 - $220,000 USD.

Compensation is determined based on several factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and skill set, geographic location, as well as internal alignment and external benchmarks.

Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time according to business needs.

This position operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms.

Job Title:

Director of GP Operations

 

Location:

Grower/Processor Facility – Erie, PA

Non-Exempt or Exempt:

Exempt

 

Reports To:

The President

Department:

Grower/Processor Operations

**Summary of the Role:**
========================

The Director of GP Operations is responsible for leading all day-to-day operations at Calypso Enterprises’ grower/processor facility in Erie, Pennsylvania, including cultivation, post-harvest, processing, inventory, and facilities. They will foster an environment that is orderly, productive, and safe while maintaining a positive culture. The Director of GP Operations will also be responsible for leading the facility’s managers and teams and ensuring compliance with company policies and procedures and all applicable Pennsylvania Department of Health regulations.

**Key Responsibilities:**
=========================

* Ensures GP production, supply levels, and inventory are in alignment with business objectives.
* Ensures managers are in compliance with company policies and procedures.
* Ensures consistent policies and procedures are developed and trained on.
* Ensures managers and teams have appropriate, accessible, and intuitive systems and structures that facilitate the efficient, effective, and safe execution of their roles and responsibilities.
* Ensures general cultural expectations are communicated to and practiced by team leaders.
* Ensures operations are optimized for profitability while maintaining the expected brand vision of quality.
* Coaches and guides teammates through analytical problem-solving and decision-making.
* Collaborates with Human Resources to mediate conflict resolutions.
* Ensures operations are compliant with OSHA safety standards.
* Directly supervises the cultivation, post-harvest, processing, inventory, and facilities managers.
* Oversees quality assurance, including laboratory testing, product holds, deviation investigations, and recall procedures.
* Ensures compliance with approved pesticide, nutrient, and integrated pest management (IPM) requirements and sanitation standards.
* Maintains and updates Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and required logs, and ensures staff complete all Department of Health-required training.
* Develops and manages the facility operating budget, approves purchasing within established limits, and reports key performance indicators to the President.
* Manages vendor and contractor relationships, including HVAC, environmental control, generator, and preventive maintenance service agreements.
* Oversees facility security, access control, and diversion prevention, and leads emergency response and incident reporting.
* Available for on-call response to facility, equipment, and security emergencies.

**Qualifications:**
===================

* A bachelor's degree in business administration, finance, management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* A minimum of 10 years of experience working in an operations role and at least five years of experience in a management or leadership capacity.
* Demonstrated success in creating creative and practical solutions to increase employee productivity and maximize profitability.
* Experience in a licensed cannabis or other regulated manufacturing environment (e.g., GMP, GACP, food, or pharmaceutical) strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience managing budgets, and multi-department teams.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Google Workspace.
* Must be 21 years of age or older.
* Must comply with all legal or company regulations for working in the industry.
* Must successfully complete a criminal background check and meet all Department of Health requirements to work at a Pennsylvania medical marijuana grower/processor.
* Valid driver’s license and the ability to travel occasionally between company locations.

**Physical and Environmental Requirements:**
============================================

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions, as required by law.

* + Prolonged periods sitting at a desk.
 + Ability to work extended shifts of up to 12 hours as needed.
 + Ability to lift, push, and pull 50 pounds.
 + Ability to sit, squat, bend, and kneel repetitively throughout a workday.
 + Ability to stand for extended periods of time.
 + Ability to work in an environment with cannabis plants, plant material, and strong odors.
 + Work can be dirty/sticky and may leave you smelling like cannabis at the end of the day.
 + Work will occur in a warehouse setting where temperatures may vary from warm to cool.
 + Work environments that include exposure to, but not limited to, fumes, dust, odors, heights, indoor AC, no AC, motion, and noise.

Management reserves the right to assign other job duties as necessary. Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

**Confidentiality:**
====================

This role has access to proprietary genetics, cultivation methods, Standard Operating Procedures, and business information. The Director of GP Operations must protect this information and comply with all company confidentiality agreements and policies.

**Diversity and Inclusion:**
============================

*Calypso Enterprises is an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate based on race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, sexual orientation, genetic information, pregnancy, sex, gender identity or expression, disability, or because of the liability for service in the armed forces of the United States or the nationality of any individual, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.*

card.title: Sr Manager, Procurement Operations - Proprietary Products
card.description:
Nutrien is a leading provider of crop inputs and services, and our business results make a positive impact on the world. Our purpose, *Feeding the Future*, is the reason we come to work each day. We’re guided by our culture of care and our core values: *We put safety first. We act with integrity. We are stronger together. We deliver with excellence.*

Through the collective expertise of our nearly 26,000 employees, we operate a world-class network of production, distribution, and ag retail facilities. We efficiently serve growers' needs and strive to provide a more profitable, sustainable, and secure future for all stakeholders. Help us raise the expectation of what an agriculture company can be and grow your career with Nutrien.

 

**Job Summary**
---------------

Senior Manager, Procurement – Proprietary Manufacturing is responsible for leading procurement strategy and execution for direct materials supporting Nutrien’s proprietary manufacturing operations, including raw materials, active ingredients, and packaging. This leader partners with Category Management, Manufacturing, Supply Planning, Research and Development, Quality, Regulatory, Finance, and Legal. This role leads site procurement teams to secure reliable supply, optimize total cost, manage risk, and align to Nutrien policies. Through strong leadership the individual will develop the procurement team, strengthen supplier performance, and deliver measurable value through disciplined sourcing, planning, and continuous improvement.

**What You'll Do:**
-------------------

* Develop and execute sourcing strategies for raw materials, active ingredients, and packaging, aligned with proprietary manufacturing, supply, quality, regulatory, and financial objectives
* Lead site buyers and procurement team members in executing strategies, purchase requirements, and supplier actions in accordance with Nutrien policies and controls
* Partner with Manufacturing and Supply Planning leadership to review forecasts, confirm material requirements, identify supply or demand gaps, and recommend adjustments to procurement plans
* Deliver sustainable cost savings, cost avoidance, working-capital improvements, and total-cost-of-ownership opportunities while protecting quality, service, safety, compliance, and continuity of supply
* Monitor commodity markets, supplier capacity, lead times, geopolitical factors, and other external conditions; translate insights into sourcing actions and risk-mitigation plans
* Lead supplier selection, competitive sourcing, negotiation, contracting, onboarding, performance management, and business reviews for assigned categories and locations
* Maintain approved suppliers, contracts, specifications, forecasts, and purchase execution within SAP S/4HANA and related procurement systems
* Develop procurement plans, budgets, forecasts, performance measures, and dashboards; communicate results, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions to business and procurement leadership
* Lead, coach, and develop team members through clear goals, performance feedback, capability building, workload prioritization, and succession planning
* Champion standardization, data quality, continuous improvement, and change initiatives that strengthen procurement discipline, collaboration with other procurement teams, and measurable business value
* Provide procurement leadership for cross-functional projects, new product introductions, formulation or packaging changes, capacity expansions, and other strategic manufacturing priorities

**What You'll Bring:**
----------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field; an advanced degree or relevant professional designations are an asset
* 10+ years of progressive experience including leadership responsibility. Deep understanding of procurement, strategic sourcing, supply chain, or materials management
* Experience in sourcing direct materials such as chemicals, active ingredients, agricultural products, packaging, or other industrial manufacturing inputs
* Proven ability to develop business strategies, negotiate complex agreements, manage supplier performance, and deliver measurable cost, working-capital, and risk-reduction results
* Strong knowledge of forecasting, material requirements planning, inventory management, source-to-contract, procure-to-pay, and supplier risk management
* Experience leading and influencing teams across multiple manufacturing locations and cross-functional organizations
* Well-developed financial and business acumen enabling cost modeling and total-cost-of-ownership analyses
* Working knowledge of SAP (S/4HANA Materials Management) and Microsoft Office suite is preferred
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, negotiation, project-management, communication, and organizational skills, with the ability to balance competing priorities and make sound decisions independently
* Demonstrated integrity, safety leadership, collaboration, accountability, commitment to continuous improvement and ability to travel as required

**What You'll Get:**
--------------------

* **Purpose-Driven Work** – Make an impact as part of a global team feeding the future and support farmers locally and around the world
* **Excellent Benefits** – Comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage, plus a retirement program with generous employer matching for your future
* **Grow Your Career** – Tuition assistance for future education and ongoing learning and training opportunities for career advancement pathways across the organization
* **Support When it Matters** – Employee Assistance Programs, inclusive leaves, and paid time for holidays, volunteering, vacation, and wellness
* **Thrive in a Strong Culture** – Guided by our core values we put safety first, act with integrity, are stronger together, and deliver with excellence in a collaborative, high-performing environment

**Compensation & Benefits:**

The salary range for this role, in Loveland, CO, is between $127,500 - $200,310. While we provide this range as general guidance, several factors are taken into consideration when making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, candidate skill set, experience and training, licensure and certifications, work location, and other business and organizational needs. Actual salary and benefits may differ based upon location.

We provide an attractive benefits package that includes comprehensive medical, dental, vision coverage, and life insurance and well as disability coverage for positions working more than 30 hours per week. In addition, we have a retirement program that encourages our employees to save for the longer term, with generous matching employer contributions. Our benefit package also demonstrates our culture of care with paid vacation, sick days and holidays as well as paid personal and maternity/parental leaves and an Employee and Family Assistance Program. Details of the benefits package will be shared in the application process.

In addition to base pay, this role is also eligible to participate in our annual incentive plan and long-term incentive plan, consistent with the terms of our program(s) where discretionary pay out of awards is reflecting components such as performance of the company and the employee. Details will be discussed through the application process.

This information is provided in compliance with applicable state equal pay and pay equity legislation and is the company's good faith and reasonable estimate of the compensation range and benefits offered for this position. The compensation offered to the successful applicant may vary based on factors including experience, skills, education, location, and other job-related reasons. Nutrien also makes internal equity a consideration in all pay decisions.

**Ready to make an impact with us? Apply today!**

The estimated salary that Indeed, Glassdoor and LinkedIn lists does not represent Nutrien's compensation structure. Nutrien is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, genetic information, and other legally protected categories.

This job will remain posted until filled. In accordance with Nutrien policies, you will be required to undergo a background check, and may be required to undergo a substance test. While we appreciate all applications we receive, only candidates under consideration will be contacted. Applicants must meet minimum age requirements, as permitted by law.

Please be advised that pre-screen interviews may be transcribed (there will be no audio or video recording) and that artificial intelligence tools may be used to summarize the transcript of the discussion. These tools will not be used to make or influence hiring decisions. Biometric identifiers and biometric information will not be captured. If you wish to request an alternative process or a reasonable accommodation, please submit a request through our Contact Us form or call 1-800-667-0403 in Canada and 1-800-667-3930 in the US to let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

Our Recruitment Process: Application > Resume Review > Pre-screen/Interview > Offer > Pre-Employment Conditions > Welcome to Nutrien

**Work for Indiana**
====================

Begin a fulfilling career with the State of Indiana by joining one of the largest employers in the state, offering a range of opportunities across 60+ agencies. At the state, you'll find competitive compensation, a robust benefits package and a commitment to work-life balance. Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

 

**About the Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV):**

The Bureau of Motor Vehicles delivers exceptional, customer focused services built on choice, innovation, and genuine care. We strive to be a trusted partner to every Hoosier by investing in our people, fostering growth, and developing future leaders who drive excellence and a strong culture of service.

 

**Role Overview:**

Located within the Policy and Programs division, the Director of Registration Operations leads the Bureau’s registration operations and special program administration, ensuring the timely and accurate issuance of vehicle and watercraft registration certificates. The position evaluates and oversees policies, procedures, and programs to drive efficiency, improve service delivery, and reduce costs, with a strong focus on customer-centered solutions. This role partners closely with the Director of Registration Compliance to support the Bureau’s mission and operational goals.

This is an onsite role in the central BMV offices at the Indiana Government Center in Indianapolis, Indiana.

The salary for this position traditionally starts at $75,010.00 but may be commensurate with education and work experience. Use our **Compensation Calculator** to view the total compensation package.

----------------------

* Responsible for strategic direction and day-to-day workflow.
* Oversees handling of branch, Branch Support, ITD calls and email, as well as Contact Center escalations.

* Wellness Rewards Program: Complete wellness activities to earn gift card rewards
* Health savings account, which includes bi-weekly state contribution
* Deferred compensation 457(b) account (similar to 401(k) plan) with employer match
* Two (2) fully-funded pension plan options
* A robust, comprehensive program of leave policies covering a variety of employee needs, including but not limited to:

* Combined 180 hours of paid vacation, personal, and sick leave time off
* 12 paid holidays, 14 on election years
* Education Reimbursement Program
* Group life insurance
* Referral Bonus program

* Qualified employer for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program
* Free Parking for most positions
Free LinkedIn Learning access

The State of Indiana is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to recruiting, selecting, developing, and promoting employees based on individual ability and job performance. Reasonable accommodations may be available to enable individuals with disabilities to complete the application and interview process as well as perform the essential functions of a role. If you require reasonable accommodations to complete this application, you can request assistance by contacting the Indiana State Personnel Department at jobs@spd.IN.gov.

 

**Nearest Major Market:** Indianapolis

card.title: VP, Operations
card.description:
**Building the people that build the world.**

With platforms in HVAC and Detection and Measurement, SPX Technologies builds innovative solutions that enable a safer, more efficient, sustainable world. Through our RiSE talent development framework, we Reach, Identify, Strengthen, and Engage our employees to support them in their continued development. We’re a global company of problem solvers, collaborators, and innovators, and our businesses build solutions that impact the world.

As part of HVAC Cooling, SPX Cooling Technologies is a leader in high quality industrial HVAC equipment used to cool large facilities like hospitals, data centers, and power plants. With cooling towers, fans, and refrigeration units, companies rely on brands like Marley, Recold, and SGS to provide comfort and mission critical and industrial cooling solutions.

 

**How You Will Make an Impact**

The Vice President, Operations is a key member of the business unit leadership team and is responsible for the global operations strategy and execution for a rapidly growing business scaling beyond $1.5 billion in annual revenue. This leader will have responsibility for a global manufacturing network of 8+ facilities and will ensure the operations organization has the capacity, capabilities, systems, talent, and processes required to support significant organic and inorganic growth.

The VP, Operations will establish and execute a scalable global operating model that delivers world-class performance across safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost, working capital, and customer service. This leader will drive greater consistency and integration across manufacturing locations while ensuring the operating footprint, capital investments, supply chain capabilities, and organizational structure are positioned to support long-term growth.

A critical priority will be building an operations organization capable of operating at significantly greater scale. The VP will develop strong plant and functional leaders, create clear accountability across the operations network, institutionalize continuous improvement, and partner closely with Commercial, Engineering, Product Management, Finance, Human Resources, and Supply Chain to translate business strategy into operational execution.

**What You Can Expect in This Role**

* **Develop and execute the global operations strategy** to support the business unit's growth, financial objectives, customer commitments, and long-term strategic plan.
* **Lead the global manufacturing network of 8+ facilities**, establishing common operating expectations, performance metrics, management systems, and accountability across locations.
* **Build the operational capacity and capabilities required to support a $2B+ business**, anticipating future requirements for facilities, equipment, automation, technology, supply chain, and talent.
* **Own manufacturing footprint and capacity strategy**, including plant utilization, expansions, greenfield/start-up operations, consolidations, transfers of production, and other network optimization opportunities.
* **Drive world-class performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost and Working Capital**, establishing clear performance expectations and corrective actions across the global operating organization.
* **Champion a culture of safety**, ensuring consistent leadership practices, risk identification, corrective actions, compliance, and continuous improvement across all manufacturing locations.
* **Establish a disciplined Lean operating system** utilizing standard work, daily management, Kaizen, problem solving, value-stream optimization, and other continuous improvement methodologies to drive sustained performance improvement.
* **Improve operational scalability and productivity** through automation, manufacturing technology, process redesign, labor productivity, plant layout optimization, and improved utilization of assets.
* **Lead operations planning and execution**, ensuring alignment between customer demand, production capacity, labor, materials, inventory, and capital requirements through disciplined SIOP/S&OP and scheduling processes.
* **Optimize material flow and working capital**, improving inventory turns, supplier performance, schedule adherence, throughput, and overall cash conversion.
* **Develop and execute the global capital strategy for Operations**, prioritizing investments based on growth requirements, productivity, safety, quality, capacity, automation, and return on invested capital.
* **Partner with Engineering and Commercial leadership** to improve manufacturability, new product introduction, quote-to-delivery execution, capacity planning, and responsiveness to changing customer requirements.
* **Support acquisition integration and business expansion**, establishing operating standards, identifying synergies, integrating newly acquired manufacturing operations, and accelerating performance improvement.
* **Build a high-performing global Operations leadership team**, strengthening succession depth and developing Plant Managers and functional leaders capable of leading increasingly large and complex operations.
* **Create a culture of accountability and operational excellence**, ensuring leaders use data, metrics, structured problem solving, and operating rhythms to identify issues early and deliver commitments.
* **Serve as a strategic advisor to the President and business leadership team**, bringing an operations perspective to growth strategy, investment decisions, customer commitments, acquisitions, organizational design, and long-range planning.

**Key Measures of Success**

Success in this role will be demonstrated through:

* Sustained improvement in employee safety and environmental performance
* World-class product quality and reduction in customer quality issues
* 95%+ on-time delivery performance and improved schedule adherence
* Year-over-year productivity and manufacturing cost improvement
* Improved inventory turns and working capital performance
* Effective deployment and return on capital investments
* Capacity and manufacturing footprint aligned with business growth
* Successful operational integration of acquisitions and new facilities
* Strong succession depth and leadership capability across Operations
* Consistent implementation of operating systems and best practices across the global manufacturing network

**What We Are Looking For**

**Required Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive operations and manufacturing leadership experience, including significant leadership of complex, multi-site operations.
* Demonstrated experience leading a large-scale global or geographically dispersed manufacturing organization.
* Experience operating within a business of significant scale and complexity, ideally $1B+ in revenue with demonstrated experience supporting substantial growth.
* Proven ability to scale manufacturing capacity, systems, processes, and organizations during periods of rapid growth.
* Demonstrated success improving safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost, and working capital performance across multiple manufacturing locations.
* Strong experience in Lean manufacturing and building sustainable continuous improvement cultures.
* Experience developing manufacturing footprint strategies including plant expansions, start-ups, consolidations, transfers, and capacity investments.
* Demonstrated success developing senior operations leaders and building strong succession pipelines.
* Experience working effectively within a matrixed, global organization and influencing across functions.
* Experience operating in both union and non-union manufacturing environments preferred.
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or manufacturing operations strongly preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

* Enterprise-level strategic thinking combined with a strong bias for execution.
* Ability to translate aggressive business growth plans into executable operations, capacity, talent, and capital strategies.
* Strong financial and business acumen with an understanding of operating margin, manufacturing economics, capital allocation, working capital, and return on investment.
* Demonstrated ability to establish operating systems, metrics, governance, and accountability across a diverse manufacturing network.
* Strong change leadership capability and demonstrated success leading organizations through significant growth and transformation.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, and influencing skills with the ability to operate effectively from the plant floor through the executive leadership team.
* Ability to identify emerging operational risks, resolve near-term issues, and simultaneously build the capabilities required for long-term growth.
* Strong knowledge of ERP, planning, manufacturing technology, automation, and data-driven operating environments.

**Education & Certifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field required.
* MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred.
* Lean/Six Sigma or comparable continuous improvement certification preferred.

**Travel & Working Environment**

* Significant domestic and international travel required to maintain strong leadership presence across the global manufacturing network.
* Regular interaction within manufacturing environments with varying levels of noise, temperature, and other plant conditions.

**How we live our culture**

Our culture is at the center of what we do and, more importantly, who we are. Our core values set a standard for how we manage ourselves, and our Leadership Model sets the standard for how we engage with each other. Whether you are an individual contributor or you lead a large team, each of us leads at SPX.

**What benefits do we offer?**

We know that the well-being of our employees is integral. Our benefits include:

* Generous and flexible paid time off including paid personal time off, caregiver, parental, and volunteer leave
* Competitive health insurance plans and 401(k) match, with benefits starting day one
* Competitive and performance-based compensation packages and bonus plans
* Educational assistance, leadership development programs, and recognition programs

**Our commitment to embrace diversity to build a culture of inclusion at SPX**

We value different backgrounds, experiences, and voices at SPX, and we are committed to challenging ourselves, openly communicating, and striving to improve every day. We believe in creating an inclusive work environment where everyone has a voice and is encouraged to realize their fullest potential.

SPX is an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer committed to making selection decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis.

card.description:
Overview:

**At Anne Arundel Dermatology we give exceptional care - to our patients and to eachother.**
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Patient First | Caring | Accountability | Trust | One Team | Growth

Founded 50+ years ago with a mission to provide the highest quality and full spectrum of medical, surgical, and esthetic skin care services to each and every one of its patients, Anne Arundel Dermatology has assembled the finest group of dermatologists in the Mid-Atlantic and Southeastern states. With 250+ clinicians and 110+ locations in 7 states, we’re thriving, growing, and looking to add talented individuals to our team!

**Why join Anne Arundel Dermatology?**

We are committed to continual training and education for our physicians and staff. We are on top of the latest developments in dermatology including ongoing research, emerging treatments, new medications and prevention methods. You can find more than just a job with Anne Arundel Dermatology. We believe in providing our new associates with intensive hands on training and long-term career growth opportunities from within.

If you are looking for a career with a busy, fast paced medical office, then joining the Anne Arundel Dermatology’s Surgery Center team is for you! We are looking for highly motivated, self-starting individuals, who work efficiently and are detail oriented, to join our team. You will not only be working alongside a large administrative team, but also with some of the top Moh’s Surgeons in the area. This is a great opportunity to be a part of our vast growing practice or an essential stepping stone for anyone looking to advance their career in the administrative side of the medical field.

**DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS SUPPORT & PROGRAM MANAGEMENT**

***Job Summary:***

The **Director of Operations Support & Program Management** provides strategic and operational leadership for enterprise operations support, project management, technology optimization, process improvement, and training. Serving as the central link between Operations, IT, Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), Clinical, Aesthetics, Marketing, and vendors, the Director removes operational barriers, translates operational needs into effective systems, workflows, and training, and ensures enterprise initiatives are implemented, adopted, and sustained.

Salary range of 140,000-160,000 annually, plus 20% bonus opportunity.

Responsibilities:

***Duties/Responsibilities:***

**Operations Support & Operational Excellence**

* Lead the Operations Support function and serve as the escalation point for complex operational and cross-functional issues.
* Establish and maintain standardized SOPs, workflows, and operational processes across the organization.
* Use process-analysis reporting to identify operational barriers and implement solutions that improve efficiency, consistency, and communication.
* Support provider onboarding and operational readiness, site moves, and other organizational changes.
* Maintain regular communication cadences with support functions, including Aesthetics and Marketing, to surface and resolve issues proactively.

**Enterprise Program & Project Management**

* Lead or oversee major cross-functional initiatives (e.g., telephony transformation, Assist Tracking/LIS transition, Medsender and AI Scribe implementations, and aesthetic online scheduling).
* Own the initiative portfolio, managing intake, prioritization, and sequencing of requests against team and field capacity.
* Establish project priorities, timelines, ownership, and deliverables using a consistent methodology (charters, stage gates, go-live readiness, hypercare, post-implementation reviews); identify risks, dependencies, resource needs, and operational impacts.
* Coordinate stakeholders across Operations, IT, clinical teams, RCM, and vendors from planning through adoption and stabilization, and manage vendor statements of work, timelines, and project budgets.
* Provide leadership with regular reporting on project progress, risks, and outcomes, including delivery measures such as on-time go-lives and adoption.

**Software Management & Digital Innovation**

* Provide strategic oversight of the operational software ecosystem (e.g., ModMed, Relatient, Klara, HubSpot, Medsender, Brevium, Birdeye, Zocdoc, and self-scheduling tools), including interface and workflow monitoring.
* Partner with IT to define system requirements, identify gaps, and implement workflow solutions; manage vendor relationships and enhancement priorities.
* Evaluate automation, integration, and digital innovation opportunities that improve the patient and provider experience.
* Establish governance for ongoing system optimization and ensure system changes are supported by sustainable workflows, training, and adoption.

**Training & Continuous Process Improvement**

* Oversee standardized training for Time of Service, new hires, providers, aesthetic processes and discounts, clinical documentation, and system or workflow changes.
* Partner with RCM and clinical leadership to address documentation deficiencies; monitor compliance and performance indicators to identify retraining needs.
* Keep training materials aligned with current SOPs and technology, and lead a culture in which process changes are implemented, measured, and refined.

**MIPS & Regulatory/Performance Initiatives**

* Lead operational coordination of MIPS activities, partnering with clinical, operational, and RCM stakeholders to operationalize requirements.
* Monitor progress, address barriers, and integrate MIPS requirements into workflows, training, documentation, and reporting.

Qualifications:

***Required Skills/Abilities:***

* Change management
* Project leadership, strategic thinking and data-driven decision making
* Process improvement and technology enablement

card.description:
Overview:

We are seeking talented, passionate individuals to join our team and help our patients live happier and healthier lives…in their homes.

The Director, Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s home care services. This role provides oversight and direction to branch leadership and is accountable for operational performance, service quality, financial results, regulatory compliance, workforce effectiveness, and growth.

The Director, Operations partners with executive leadership, branch leaders, clinical teams, and other functional departments to drive consistent execution of operational strategies, identify opportunities for improvement, and deliver high-quality, patient-centered care. This role serves as a key leader in developing scalable processes, strengthening branch performance, and supporting the organization’s overall growth objectives.

What We Offer\*:

We know that, to be the best place for our patients, we must be the best place to work for our employees. We offer the 
following to our employees:

* Be part of a unique healthcare company where we can help those in our communities who need our help the

most 

* Flexible hours/work-life balance
* Competitive pay
* Paid on a weekly basis
* Medical/dental/vision/life insurance
* Paid holidays/PTO/401(k) match
* Career growth opportunities
* Great and collaborative work environment

Responsibilities:

What You Will Do:

**Operational Leadership**

* Provide leadership and oversight for the day-to-day operations of assigned home care branches and service areas.
* Lead, coach, and hold branch leaders accountable for operational, financial, clinical, service, and workforce performance.
* Establish and monitor operational goals, performance metrics, and action plans to improve results.
* Standardize processes and workflows across branches to improve efficiency, consistency, service quality, and scalability.
* Identify operational barriers and implement solutions that improve client service, employee effectiveness, and overall performance.
* Partner with other service lines and support functions to ensure effective coordination and execution of organizational initiatives.

**Financial & Business Performance**

* Manage branch budgets and financial performance in partnership with Finance and operational leadership.
* Monitor revenue, labor costs, productivity, staffing levels, utilization, and other key performance indicators.
* Identify opportunities to improve profitability, control costs, and optimize operational resources.
* Analyze performance trends and develop corrective action plans when branches or service areas are not meeting established goals.

**Strategic Planning & Growth**

* Partner with the Vice President, Operations and executive leadership to develop and execute strategic plans for market growth and service expansion.
* Identify opportunities to expand services, strengthen market presence, and improve client access.
* Monitor industry, competitor, regulatory, and market trends and recommend strategies to address emerging opportunities and challenges.
* Evaluate and implement technology, systems, and other tools that improve operational efficiency, communication, and client experience.
* Support organizational growth initiatives, including new market development and mergers and acquisitions as assigned.

**People Leadership**

* Build a high-performing culture focused on accountability, collaboration, service excellence, and employee engagement.
* Recruit, onboard, develop, coach, and evaluate assigned leaders and staff.
* Partner with Human Resources on talent acquisition, employee relations, performance management, retention, workforce planning, and leadership development.
* Establish clear performance expectations and provide ongoing coaching and feedback to direct reports.
* Identify staffing and leadership needs and develop strategies to support workforce stability and growth.

**Quality, Compliance & Risk Management**

* Ensure operations comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, payer requirements, and organizational policies.
* Partner with Clinical, Compliance, Quality, and other functional leaders to maintain high standards of care and operational compliance.
* Monitor quality indicators, client outcomes, service delivery, and regulatory requirements and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Ensure appropriate policies, procedures, controls, and processes are implemented and consistently followed.
* Support regulatory surveys, audits, investigations, and corrective action plans as required.

**Client & Community Relations**

* Promote a culture of exceptional customer service and patient-centered care.
* Monitor client and family satisfaction and ensure concerns are addressed promptly and appropriately.
* Build and maintain relationships with clients, families, healthcare providers, referral sources, community organizations, and other key stakeholders.
* Represent the organization at community events, industry functions, and other external forums as appropriate.
* Partner with marketing, community relations, and other teams to strengthen referral relationships and market presence.

**Leadership & Collaboration**

* Partner effectively with Finance, Human Resources, Clinical, Compliance, Revenue Cycle, Marketing, and other departments to achieve organizational objectives.
* Communicate operational priorities, performance results, and emerging issues to the Vice President, Operations and executive leadership.
* Promote accountability, continuous improvement, and effective communication across the organization.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

 
Qualifications:

Qualifications:

* Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Nursing, or a related field required; master’s degree preferred.
* Five or more years of progressive healthcare operations or management experience, with demonstrated leadership responsibility.
* Experience managing multi-site, multi-branch, or geographically dispersed healthcare operations preferred.
* Previous home care, home health, personal care, hospice, or other post-acute healthcare experience strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience managing budgets, financial performance, operational metrics, and performance improvement initiatives.
* Experience leading and developing managers and other operational staff.
* Working knowledge of applicable home care regulations, reimbursement and billing practices, quality standards, and industry trends.

* Eligibility for certain benefits may depend on employment status

CareRing Health is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other classification protected by applicable law.

card.title: Program Operations Director - Epidemiology
card.description:
Overview:

Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. Based in Seattle, Fred Hutch is the only National Cancer Institute-designated cancer center in Washington.

With a track record of global leadership in bone marrow transplantation, HIV/AIDS prevention, immunotherapy and COVID-19 vaccines, Fred Hutch has earned a reputation as one of the world’s leading cancer, infectious disease and biomedical research centers. Fred Hutch operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world’s deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.

At Fred Hutch we value collaboration, compassion, determination, excellence, innovation, integrity and respect. Our mission is directly tied to the humanity, dignity and inherent value of each employee, patient, community member and supporter. Our commitment to learning across our differences and similarities make us stronger. We seek employees who bring different and innovative ways of seeing the world and solving problems.

The Cancer Epidemiology Program, as one of five scientific programs within the Public Health Sciences Division, is focused on reducing cancer incidence, progression, mortality, and sequalae through the identification of risk (or protective) factors, the elucidation of underlying biologic mechanisms, and the translation of discoveries into prevention strategies. The program includes more than a dozen core faculty based at Fred Hutch, plus affiliated faculty from the University of Washington, as well as a large number of research staff, ranging from program assistants, interviewers, medical record abstractors, project coordinators, study managers, and statistical research associates.

The **Program Operations Director** is responsible for the overall program activities and administrative operations including strategy, financial, personnel, grants and contracts, regulatory and administrative functions for a broad program comprised of multiple research groups. This position requires an understanding of sponsored research, regulatory requirements, performance management, administrative systems, program management and broad experience with business functions and systems, including program leadership, strategic planning, budgeting, fiscal analysis, human resources management and communication. This position reports to the Epidemiology Program Head.

Responsibilities:

This position works with overarching guidance from program leadership, Principal Investigators (PIs) and the Division’s Associate Vice President to independently plan and oversee administrative operations for the program research portfolio. The Program Operation Director manages the administrative team and oversees all day-to-day operational and administrative responsibilities for the program, sets functional strategies and objectives on operational plans that align with overall Division and organizational strategies, and provides input to Division-level strategic planning.

General Program Operations and Administration:

* Lead the program administration team.
* Support the Program Head in developing the program strategic plan and annual reporting requirements, planning and attending faculty meetings, workshops and retreats.
* Work in partnership with Center and Division administrative teams to ensure successful implementation and integration of programs and center-wide initiatives; foster cross-functional collaboration.
* Participate in Center and Division-led meetings, committees and special projects.
* Direct and provide leadership to the Epidemiology Program study managers, including ensuring there are regular research staff meetings, where information on new policies and practices relevant to the Program can be communicated, disseminated, and implemented.
* Manage space usage and allocation including planning for future uses and adapting to changing faculty/research needs.
* Partner with Communications Team to develop and maintain website and content development.

Financial and Data Management:

* Oversee general financial operations for the program including forecasting, management, reporting, reconciliations, purchasing and vendor contract management for sponsored, non-sponsored and foundation funded projects.
* Oversee the preparation, management, and monitoring of the Program's annual budget and faculty funding needs. Perform cost analysis and obtain data needed for requests. Justify and advocate for budget requests directly with Division senior leadership, Finance, and Compensation departments.
* In collaboration with the Senior Research Administration Manager, oversee grant activities including grant preparation, budget development/management, forecasting, reporting and report tools development.

Faculty Support:

* Coordinate faculty recruiting activities for the program and support the Division office in administration and faculty promotions
* Identify opportunities and assist faculty in cultivating and managing relationships within and outside Fred Hutch.
* Assist the Fred Hutch Philanthropy and Marketing departments in cooperation with the Division to ensure all achievements and donor relationships are appropriately highlighted and managed
* Manage and maintain the faculty grant library, program documentation, policy materials and support recurring reporting needs.
* Seek new funding opportunities for the program as appropriate

HR Management:

* Facilitate the annual staff performance management and merit review process.
* Assist the Program Head and Division with faculty HR matters including promotions, appointment changes, onboarding, offboarding and the annual merit review process.
* Advise and assist faculty and study managers in developing study team structures, submissions of employment requisitions and personnel actions, classification review, disciplinary actions, trainee and graduate student inquiries and staff training and development planning.

Qualifications:

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, public administration or a related field.
* Minimum of 8-10 years of federal research administration management experience.
* Minimum of 3-5 years of supervisory and leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success managing and engaging diverse stakeholders across a complex research portfolio.
* Experience with translating science into strategy in creating and executing strategic plans.
* Strong communication and budgetary skills.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Master's degree.
* 3-5 years of experience in supporting faculty in an academic environment.
* Experience in identifying areas for process improvement and implementing associated change management strategies to successfully rollout and sustain initiatives.
* Robust budget management and forecasting skills.
* Experience in leading a diverse team, thinking creatively and globally, projecting future needs, and being attuned to the day-to-day program operations.
* Flexible and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities.
* Exemplary organizational skills, attention to detail and service orientation.
* Demonstrated ability to successfully operate in and lead a complex, matrixed, and high-performing organization.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong background in data analytics and visualization.
* Advanced experience with Microsoft suite (e.g., Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint).
* Ability to create a positive work culture.
* Flexibility and adaptability.
* Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment.
* Outstanding interpersonal skills.
* Positive attitude and sense of humor.

The annual base salary range for this position is from $123,968 to $195,915, and pay offered will be based on experience and qualifications. 
 
Although Fred Hutch is not sponsoring most H-1B visas at this time, candidates who already hold an H-1B sponsored by another organization and are currently in the U.S. may be eligible for this position. 
 
Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center offers employees a comprehensive benefits package designed to enhance health, well-being, and financial security. Benefits include medical/vision, dental, flexible spending accounts, life, disability, retirement, family life support, employee assistance program, onsite health clinic, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation (12-22 days per year), paid sick leave (12-25 days per year), paid holidays (13 days per year), and paid parental leave (up to 4 weeks).

Additional Information: We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and Vietnam Era Veterans Readjustment Assistance Act (VEVRAA) Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, ancestry, national origin, sex, age, disability (physical or mental), marital or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, political ideology, or membership in any other legally protected class. We desire priority referrals of protected veterans. If due to a disability you need assistance/and or a reasonable accommodation during the application or recruiting process, please send a request to Human Resources at hrops@fredhutch.org or by calling 206-667-4700.
